questions.text: At what rate of simple interest per annum will a sum of money double itself in 8 years?
questions.solution: Shortcut: For a sum to double at simple interest, Rate = 100/Time. Here Time = 8 years → Rate = 100/8 = 12.5%. Full: SI = P×R×T/100; since Amount = 2P, SI = P → P = P×R×8/100 → R = 100/8 = 12.5%.

questions.text: A is the brother of B. C is the daughter of B. D is the brother of C. How is D related to A?
questions.solution: B is A's sibling, so B's children are A's nephews/nieces. C and D are B's children, making D the nephew of A. Shortcut: draw a quick family tree: A—B (siblings), B→C,D (children) ⇒ D is nephew of A.

questions.text: Identify the part of speech of the underlined word in the sentence: "She quickly ran to the store."
questions.solution: Shortcut: Words ending in '-ly' that modify a verb are usually adverbs. Full solution: 'Quickly' describes how she ran, modifying the verb 'ran'; therefore it functions as an adverb. The other options (adjective, verb, noun) do not fit the syntactic role.

questions.text: Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error. The quality of the mangoes were not good enough to be exported.
questions.solution: Shortcut: Ignore the prepositional phrase 'of the mangoes'. The main subject is 'The quality' (singular), so the verb must be singular 'was', not plural 'were'. Step-by-step: 1. Identify the subject: 'The quality'. 2. Identify the verb: 'were'. 3. 'Quality' is a singular noun. 4. The phrase 'of the mangoes' is a modifier and does not decide the verb number. 5. Singular subject requires singular verb 'was'. 6. Segment 'were' contains the error.

questions.text: Who among the following founded the 'Servants of India Society' in 1905?
questions.solution: Gopal Krishna Gokhale founded the Servants of India Society in Pune in 1905 to train national missionaries for the service of India. Shortcut: Associate leaders with their organizations: Tilak (Home Rule League), Lajpat Rai (Punjab National Bank/Servants of People Society), Pal (Bande Mataram), Gokhale (Servants of India Society). Step-by-step: Gokhale, a moderate leader and mentor to Gandhi, believed in constitutional agitation and social service, leading to the formation of this society.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'HEART' is written as 'SVZIG'. How will 'WORLD' be written in that code?
questions.solution: The code uses Atbash cipher: each letter is replaced by its mirror in the alphabet (A↔Z, B↔Y, …). Applying this to WORLD: W→D, O→L, R→I, L→O, D→W → DLIOW. Shortcut: memorize the mirror pairs or use position 27−p.

questions.text: What is the unit digit of (6^45 + 4^32)?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Unit digit of 6^n is always 6; unit digit of 4^n cycles 4,6 for odd/even n. 45 → 6^45 ends with 6; 32 even → 4^32 ends with 6. Sum unit digit = 6+6=12 → 2. Full: 6^any = …6; 4^2=16→6, cycle length 2, 32 even →6; 6+6=12 → unit digit 2.

questions.text: Under which Schedule of the Indian Constitution are provisions related to the Anti-Defection Law enshrined?
questions.solution: The 10th Schedule was added by the 52nd Amendment Act, 1985, and contains provisions for disqualification on grounds of defection. Shortcut: Memorize the sequence of key Schedules: 8th (Languages), 9th (Validation of Acts), 10th (Anti-Defection), 11th (Panchayats). Step-by-step: The Anti-Defection law was enacted to combat political instability; it is constitutionally placed in the 10th Schedule.

questions.text: In the following letter series, each term follows a specific pattern: A, C, F, J, O, ?. Which letter comes next?
questions.solution: The differences between consecutive letters are +2, +3, +4, +5; thus the next difference is +6. O (15) +6 = 21 → U. Shortcut: observe the increment increasing by 1 each step.

questions.text: Deficiency of which vitamin causes 'Rickets' in children?
questions.solution: Rickets is a bone deformity disease caused by Vitamin D deficiency, which impairs calcium and phosphate absorption. Shortcut: Use the deficiency mnemonic: Vit A → Night Blindness; Vit B1 → Beri Beri; Vit C → Scurvy; Vit D → Rickets (Bones/Calcium). Step-by-step: Vitamin D (Calciferol) is essential for bone mineralization; its lack in growing children leads to soft, weak bones characteristic of Rickets.

questions.text: A train 180 metres long crosses a platform 220 metres long in 20 seconds. What is the speed of the train in km/h?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Speed (km/h) = (Total distance in metres ÷ Time in seconds) × 18/5. Total distance = 180+220 = 400 m, time = 20 s → (400/20)×18/5 = 20×3.6 = 72 km/h. Full: Distance = 400 m, speed = 400/20 = 20 m/s; converting: 20 × 18/5 = 72 km/h.

questions.text: The cost price of 10 articles is equal to the selling price of 8 articles. What is the profit percentage?
questions.solution: Shortcut: If CP of x articles = SP of y articles, profit% = ((x-y)/y)×100. Here x=10, y=8 → (2/8)×100 = 25%. Full: Let CP of 1 article = ₹1, then CP of 10 = ₹10 = SP of 8 → SP of 1 = ₹10/8 = ₹1.25. Profit = ₹0.25 on ₹1 → 25%.

questions.text: 'Indira Point', the southernmost point of the territory of India, is located in which Union Territory?
questions.solution: Indira Point is situated on Great Nicobar Island in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands. Shortcut: Eliminate options by geography: Kanyakumari is the southernmost mainland point (Tamil Nadu); Lakshadweep lies in the Arabian Sea (West); Puducherry and Daman & Diu are coastal enclaves on the mainland. Only Andaman & Nicobar extends far south into the Bay of Bengal. Step-by-step: The territory of India includes islands; the Nicobar group is the southernmost, making Andaman & Nicobar Islands the correct UT.

questions.text: Select the appropriate preposition to fill the blank: "He is good ___ mathematics."
questions.solution: Shortcut: The collocation 'good at' is standard for skills/subjects; eliminate 'in', 'on', 'with' as they are not used with 'good' in this sense. Full solution: The adjective 'good' pairs with the preposition 'at' when referring to proficiency in a subject (e.g., good at math). Hence the correct choice is 'at', which is option C (index 2).

questions.text: Ravi walks 12 km North, then turns right and walks 5 km. What is the straight‑line distance between his final position and the starting point?
questions.solution: The path forms a right triangle with legs 12 km and 5 km. By Pythagoras, distance = √(12²+5²) = √(144+25) = √169 = 13 km. Shortcut: recognise the 5‑12‑13 Pythagorean triplet.
